study_material.title: Digital Marketing & Social Media
study_material.introduction: Most placement-season marketing roles involve digital channels day one. This topic covers the core digital marketing vocabulary - funnels, paid vs. owned vs. earned media, the key metrics recruiters expect you to know, and how to reason about channel selection.
learning_objectives: Explain the marketing funnel (Awareness, Consideration, Conversion, Retention/Loyalty)
Distinguish paid, owned, and earned media with an example of each
Define CAC, CTR, conversion rate and ROAS
Explain the difference between SEO and SEM
Reason about which channel fits which funnel stage

concepts.heading: 1. The Marketing Funnel
concepts.body: Awareness (customer learns the brand exists - broad reach channels like social ads, video), Consideration (customer evaluates options - content marketing, reviews, comparison content), Conversion (customer purchases - retargeting ads, promotions, strong product pages), Retention/Loyalty (customer returns and advocates - email, loyalty programs, community). Different channels and messages are appropriate at different funnel stages - a common interview mistake is using a broad-awareness message at the conversion stage, or vice versa.

concepts.heading: 2. Paid, Owned and Earned Media
concepts.body: Paid media: you pay for placement (search ads, social ads, influencer sponsorships) - fast, scalable, but stops when spend stops. Owned media: channels the brand controls (website, email list, app, blog) - builds a long-term asset, but requires effort to build an audience. Earned media: publicity you don't pay for or control directly (press coverage, organic social shares, word of mouth) - highest credibility, but not directly controllable. A healthy digital strategy usually blends all three rather than relying on one.

concepts.heading: 3. SEO vs. SEM
concepts.body: SEO (Search Engine Optimization): improving a website's organic (unpaid) ranking in search results through content quality, keywords, backlinks and technical site health - slow to build, but free traffic once ranked and compounds over time. SEM (Search Engine Marketing): paying for ads that appear in search results (e.g. Google Ads), typically priced per click - immediate visibility, but traffic stops the moment spend stops.

concepts.heading: 4. Core Digital Metrics
concepts.body: CTR (Click-Through Rate): clicks / impressions - measures how compelling an ad or link is. Conversion Rate: conversions / total visitors - measures how well a page/flow turns interest into action. CAC (Customer Acquisition Cost): total marketing+sales spend / new customers acquired - what it costs to win one customer. ROAS (Return on Ad Spend): revenue generated / amount spent on ads - direct profitability signal for a campaign. CAC should always be evaluated against Customer Lifetime Value (LTV); a low CAC alone doesn't guarantee profitability if LTV is even lower.

formulas: CAC = total acquisition spend / number of new customers acquired
ROAS = revenue from ads / ad spend
shortcut_methods: Map any digital channel question to the funnel first: is this an awareness, consideration, conversion, or retention play? That instantly narrows down which channels and metrics are relevant.
If CAC is mentioned, always ask about LTV in the same breath - CAC alone can't tell you if acquisition is profitable
SEO = free but slow to build; SEM = fast but stops the instant you stop paying - a good default answer for 'which should we use' is both, at different time horizons
common_mistakes: Treating paid, owned and earned media as interchangeable rather than complementary
Quoting CAC as a success metric without comparing it to LTV
Confusing SEO (organic/free) with SEM (paid search ads) - they're often literally displayed on the same search results page but work completely differently
study_material.summary: Digital marketing interview questions almost always reduce to: which funnel stage are we solving for, which media type (paid/owned/earned) fits it, and which metric proves it worked - CAC and ROAS being the two recruiters ask about most.
quick_revision_notes: Paid = pay for placement; Owned = brand-controlled channel; Earned = free publicity/word of mouth
SEO = organic/free/slow; SEM = paid search ads/fast/stops when spend stops
CAC must be judged against LTV, never in isolation

practice_questions.question: A broad social media ad campaign introducing a new brand to people who've never heard of it targets which funnel stage?
practice_questions.explanation: Introducing the brand to a new audience for the first time is the top-of-funnel Awareness stage.

practice_questions.question: A positive news article about a company, written by an independent journalist without payment, is an example of:
practice_questions.explanation: Publicity that isn't paid for or directly controlled by the brand - like unsolicited press coverage - is earned media.

practice_questions.question: Which of the following best describes SEO?
options: Improving unpaid, organic search ranking through content and site quality
Paying for ads to appear at the top of search results
practice_questions.correct_answer: Improving unpaid, organic search ranking through content and site quality
practice_questions.explanation: SEO is about improving organic (unpaid) search rankings, unlike SEM which is paid search advertising.

practice_questions.question: A campaign spends Rs. 50,000 and acquires 500 new customers. What is the CAC?
practice_questions.explanation: CAC = total spend / new customers = 50,000 / 500 = Rs. 100 per customer.

practice_questions.question: A startup proudly reports a CAC of Rs. 200 per customer. What critical piece of information is missing to judge whether this is good?
options: The customer's lifetime value (LTV) - CAC alone doesn't show profitability
The color scheme of the landing page
practice_questions.correct_answer: The customer's lifetime value (LTV) - CAC alone doesn't show profitability
practice_questions.explanation: CAC only tells you the cost to acquire a customer - it must be compared against LTV (the revenue that customer generates over time) to know whether the spend is actually profitable.
